results.title: Space Agent AI Might Be The Cleanest Open Source Agent Workspace Yet – Goldie Agency
results.content:
Even so, usability matters more than many people admit.

A tool that feels smooth often wins over a tool that feels frustrating, even if the frustrating one looks stronger on paper.

That is especially true for wider adoption.

Most people do not want to spend their week debugging a system they only wanted to use.

They want something that works.

They want something they understand.

They want something that feels stable enough to trust.

That is why Space Agent AI stands out. [...] OpenClaw can be powerful, but it often feels rougher, more technical, and easier to break.

Hermes can also do impressive things, but the workflow can still feel heavier than what many users want.

Space Agent AI appears to focus harder on usability.

That does not automatically make it the best choice in every situation.

Some users will still prefer a more technical stack.

Others will choose based on specific features, integrations, or preferences around models. [...] One bad move can clutter a workspace, break a useful setup, or create extra cleanup that kills momentum.

That is where trust disappears.

If users feel like one wrong step will ruin everything, they become more cautious.

They stop experimenting.

They use the tool less.

Rollback changes that.

If Space Agent AI lets users return to an earlier point, the whole product feels safer.

That safety is not flashy, but it matters a lot.

It lowers the emotional cost of testing new ideas.

results.title: AI Workspace: How People and Agents Work Together
results.content:
Most AI features your team uses stand on the sidelines of real work. A summarize button here, a chatbot in the sidebar there. Individually, they’re useful, but they can’t see how a delayed design asset in one team creates a deadline risk in another. And they can’t act on that connection either — they just wait to be asked. [...] An AI workspace gets more valuable when multiple departments use it. Agents in one area act on data generated by another, creating one connected workspace.

Here’s how that plays out across the functions you manage every day, and what each agent does inside a live workflow.

### Department-by-department: where agents deliver the most value [...] The downfall that happens between strategy and execution is usually a coordination and capacity problem rather than a planning issue. And the platform you choose is integral to overcoming it.

Before committing to any AI workspace, ask whether:

- agents and people share the same data layer
- governance controls are built in from the start
- your whole workforce will commit to using it.

results.content:
Workspace Agents are shared AI agents that a team can build once, use together inside ChatGPT or Slack, and then refine over time through conversational corrections and persistent memory. The official definition, taken from the OpenAI launch post, describes them as "shared agents that can handle complex tasks and long-running workflows across tools and teams." The difference compared to the older Custom GPTs, which since 2023 allowed users to create personalized assistants but were largely [...] Heads up: Claude Code remains oriented toward the individual developer's work, while OpenAI's Workspace Agents target the work of non-technical teams. Comparing them head to head as "AI agents" risks being misleading, because they occupy two different quadrants of the matrix between individual/team and technical/business.

## Comparison with Microsoft: Copilot Studio and Agent 365 [...] ## Conclusions

Operational verdict: Workspace Agents are OpenAI's most aggressive move yet to stake a claim in the enterprise AI agent market, but they do not win it alone. April 22, 2026 will go down as the day five giants challenged each other in parallel, and the real victory will belong to whoever integrates best into the team's existing workflow.

Unlike standard ChatGPT interactions, these agents maintain shared context across team members, enabling seamless handoffs for tasks like data analysis, report generation, or integrations with external APIs and tools. They run asynchronously in the cloud, processing long-running jobs without tying up user sessions, and incorporate robust [...] More recently, OpenAI's o1-preview model in late 2024 demonstrated advanced reasoning for agent-like behaviors, scoring 83% on complex coding challenges compared to GPT-4o's 70%.
